title: A low surrogate escape before a high surrogate escape
notes: A surrogate code point is not a character (c-printable [1] excludes xD800 to xDFFF), and only a high surrogate escape directly followed by a low surrogate escape encodes one (RFC 8259 section 7, read by the kit as in the pair case), so any other use of a surrogate escape names no character and is an error. Loose mode needs any error; strict needs the syntax category. Here the low surrogate comes first, so neither half belongs to a pair.

provenance.reference: A decoder that accepted a surrogate escape that is not half of a pair and produced an invalid string or a replacement character.
